text:
incident-bot: Pager: p99 tail latency spike for streaming endpoints in eu-west2 detected (alert: streaming_tail_p99 > 2.5s). Rolling customer impact: some responses stalling / clients seeing long tail times. Please ACK and triage.

ops-oncall (pager): ACKing. I'm on it — grabbing logs and tracing.

Maya: I'm seeing a sharp jump in TLS handshake retransmits on the eu-west2 egress NAT path, starts ~2026-03-15T03:12Z. Packet loss on cross-AZ path ~1.8% from probes, conntrack entries hitting high-water on nat nodes.

Derek: Confirmed from VPC flow logs — SYN retransmits increased and flows are being NAT translated across AZ B -> AZ C. There's a path MTU flap in one of the intermediary gateways. Also seeing ECN marking spikes correlated to the same window.

Leah: Customer-facing: two large customers reported timeouts for streaming completions. CS says about ~120 active streams had stalls, ~30 aborted sessions.

Sanjay: Quick ask: can we fail traffic to an alternate egress in the region while we investigate? We should also consider temporarily lowering model max_tokens for streaming to shorten tails.

Maya: Working on a mitigation plan: 1) divert egress for affected subnets to az-2-egress (non-default) via BGP reroute for eu-west2-*/redwood-ml subnets; 2) scale NAT fleet (spin up 2 additional nat-proxies); 3) bump conntrack max on nat-proxies by +50% and roll a new kernel param; 4) enable short-term TCP retransmit tuning (reduce timeouts).

Derek: I'll open a routing change with netops to shift egress. Doing a dry-run: `ip route replace` on test node, verifying no session break for ongoing streams. If we can gracefully steer new sessions, that should cut handshake failures.

ops-oncall (pager): Performing traffic steering now to az-2-egress for the impacted subnets. Pushing change to 10% of traffic first. Watch metrics.

incident-bot: Change deployed: egress reroute 10% -> az-2-egress (change-id: CHG-8271).

Leah: Noted. CS updated customers with a short note about degraded streaming performance and we're applying mitigations.

Maya: After 10% switch: handshake retransmits down ~20%, p99 improved ~15% for those routed flows. Scaling nat-proxies now.

Derek: ECN marking still high on original path; looks like queue pressure on an interzone router. Netops says there's an ongoing maintenance on provider-side, will confirm ETA.

Sanjay: While nat-proxies scale, can we also trigger a model-fallback route? For some latency-sensitive customers, switch to a low-latency quantized variant (v2-q8) in eu-west2 so smaller outputs finish faster if a stall happens.

Maya: Good idea. Initiating canary: route 20% of affected customers to v2-q8 fallback. This is configured in the routing policy with immediate fallback and no retries to heavy models.

ops-oncall (pager): NAT scaling complete (+2 proxies). Conntrack bump applied on proxies. Kernel param: `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` increased from 524288 -> 786432 and `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` lowered from 432000 -> 120000 for faster turnover.

incident-bot: Monitoring: p99 latency moving down region-wide. Streaming stalls still present but reduced.

Maya: After full failover (progressing from 10% to 60% then 100%) the overall p99 for streaming endpoints improved from 3.8s -> 1.7s. Customer aborts dropped to ~4 sessions. Good partial mitigation.

Derek: We have confirmation: provider maintenance causing transient packet reordering and ECN burst which amplified queueing on our default egress link. Netops opened ticket with ISP (TKT-99827). Estimated fix in 45-90m.

Leah: Oncall handoff note: I'm going offline in 20m. Handoff to Maya. Summary for next oncall: root cause seems to be provider-side interzone router causing ECN-driven queueing + conntrack saturation on our nat nodes; mitigations applied: egress reroute, nat scaling, conntrack tuning, canary model fallback. Ongoing items: ISP ticket & postmortem, customer comms.

Maya: Taking over. Confirmed I have runbooks and CHG-8271 link. I'll monitor for 1h and keep CS updated.

Sanjay: Also add an immediate playbook task: enable streaming keepalive probes (shorter function call heartbeats) for long-lived streams to avoid silent stalls while we wait for ISP fix.

ops-oncall (pager): Enabling streaming keepalive probes in config for impacted app routes (rolling).

incident-bot: Note: automated alert threshold lowered to catch early handshake jitter; new alert (streaming_handshake_jitter_eu-west2) created to notify on 10% retransmit increase in 5m.

Derek: Followup actions for postmortem: 1) validate conntrack tuning didn't regress other workloads; 2) add egress path diversity to infra diagram and simulate failover in staging; 3) evaluate ECN handling heuristics (reduce sensitivity or shape earlier).

Leah: CS prepping a concise customer update for the affected tenants with timeline and mitigations. SRE to approve copy.

Maya: Handing to night shift: I'm leaving this in a steady state: traffic on alternate egress, nat proxies scaled, model fallback in effect, keepalives enabled. Will escalate if ISP indicates longer outage.

cs-ops: Thanks team — I've queued the customer note and will ping legal for any contractual exposure.

ops-oncall (pager): logging final check: no new pager alerts in last 12m, p99 stable ~1.6s. Closing urgent paging channel but leaving thread open for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
